title: A good product can still fail
hook: Same product, same price: one launch dies, one takes off.

knows: that a product is worth buying if its value exceeds its price
doesNotKnow: that when a product's value grows with the number of users, the same product and price can collapse to zero or reach most of the market depending on where it starts

misconception: A good product at a fair price will eventually find its users, whatever its starting share.
objective: The learner can explain that with network effects there is a tipping point: a launch below critical mass shrinks to nothing, and one above it grows to a large stable share.

claims.text: In this toy market, next round's share is 1 minus 0.16 divided by this round's share (and 0 when the share is 0.16 or less).
claims.source: Person x (x from 0 to 1) has value (1 - x) * s and joins when (1 - x) * s > 0.16, i.e. x < 1 - 0.16 / s. The fraction of people with x below that is 1 - 0.16 / s when s > 0.16, else 0. Demo.tsx next(). Stated model, not an empirical claim.

claims.text: The curve meets the diagonal at 0%, 20% and 80%, where a round changes nothing.
claims.source: Solve z = 1 - 0.16 / z: z^2 - z + 0.16 = 0, roots (1 +- sqrt(1 - 0.64)) / 2 = 0.8 and 0.2; z = 0 is also fixed (share 0 gives 0). Re-run in node: roots 0.8, 0.2.

claims.text: A launch at 18% falls to 11% and then to 0 (two rounds); a launch at 25% goes 25, 36, 56, 71, 78, 79, 80 percent and settles near 80% in six rounds (stopping when a round moves less than half a point).
claims.source: Node run of next(): 0.18 -> 0.111 -> 0; 0.25 -> 0.360, 0.556, 0.712, 0.775, 0.794, 0.798 (stop: change 0.004 < 0.005). Displayed shares are rounded to whole percent. Starts 1..100% all classified: below 20 die, above 20 end at 80% (no misclassification).

claims.text: With network effects a product has a tipping point, a critical mass: below it the share shrinks each round, above it the share grows (19% falls to 16% then 0; 21% rises to 24%, 33%, 51%, 69% and on to 80%).
claims.source: Easley & Kleinberg 2010, ch. 17 (network effects and critical mass); section 17.2 to 17.4 unconfirmed (proxy fetch failed, human check against the free PDF). Numbers: node run 0.19 -> 0.158 -> 0; 0.21 -> 0.238, 0.328, 0.512, 0.688, 0.767, ... 0.799.

claims.text: The 20% point is unstable (a start just off it moves away) and 0% and 80% are stable (a start near them moves toward them).
claims.source: Slope of next(s) = 0.16 / s^2: 4 at s = 0.2 (greater than 1, errors grow), 0.25 at s = 0.8 (less than 1, errors shrink); 0 is stable because any share up to 0.16 gives 0 in one round. Node check of every whole-percent start 1..100 agrees.

claims.text: The numbers ($0.16 price, value (1 - x) times the share, rounds) are made up for the toy model and are not a forecast for any real product.
claims.source: Stated modelling assumption; the card names no real product. The rounds are a story about how people react to others.

recall.question: A product is worth its price to many people, but only 10% of the market uses it, and its value grows with the number of users. What usually happens?
options: It can shrink to nothing, because it starts below its critical mass
It always climbs, because it is worth its price
recall.why: With network effects, a launch below the tipping point loses users each round, because the product is worth less to later people. Only a start above critical mass grows.

references.note: network effects and critical mass; section unconfirmed, ask said 17.2-17.4
